plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value of $5 ensures I only win when profitable (value exceeds the price I'd pay) and maximizes expected profit. I'll bid my true value.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. The dominant strategy in such auctions is to bid exactly my true value, since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win. Bidding above my value risks negative profit if I win at a price above value; bidding below risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to adjust for, truthful bidding at $40 maximizes expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and you never pay more than your value. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior round history to adjust for, the theoretically optimal and safest strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $32.
